The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has outlined the legal frameworks governing environmental protection, mining activities and the restoration of degraded lands and water bodies in Ghana.
EPA Chief Executive Officer, Prof. Nana Ama Browne Klutse, said the agency’s mandate was grounded in the 1992 Constitution and several laws, including the Environmental Protection Act, 2025 (Act 1124).
“Article 36(9) talks about the fact that the protection of our environment is a state responsibility. We go to Section 41(k), it also talks about the fact that citizens are also responsible for protecting the environment,” she said.
Speaking at the launch of the Water Restoration and Management Framework in Ho on Thursday, she explained that Section 2 of Act 1124 mandates the EPA to regulate, protect and coordinate environmental matters, while Section 3 empowers it to enforce environmental protection requirements.
She said Section 29 of the Act requires environmental assessment for undertakings likely to have adverse effects on the environment.
“This means that EPA has the right to visit these undertakings to assess, to monitor and to ensure that they are complying with the environmental requirements,” Prof. Browne Klutse stated.
She noted that the requirements apply to activities such as mining, land reclamation and water restoration, which must undergo the necessary screening, assessment and permitting processes.
On mining, she cited the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703), explaining that mining companies must obtain the necessary authorisations from the EPA and Forestry Commission before commencing operations.
She also explained that land reclamation is treated as a mining-related activity because it involves the soil and the effects of mining, requiring the involvement of relevant regulatory institutions.
Prof. Browne Klutse further identified the Water Resources Commission Act, 1996 (Act 522), the Ghana Hydrological Authority Act, 2022, and the Local Governance Act, 2016 (Act 936), among other laws, as part of the legal framework supporting water restoration and environmental management.
She said the various laws provide the basis for collaboration among institutions, including the EPA, Minerals Commission, Forestry Commission, Water Resources Commission and local authorities, to ensure effective environmental protection and restoration.
